questions.q: What is a sensitivity label in Fabric and Power BI?
options: A Microsoft Purview classification tag (e.g. Public, General, Confidential, Highly Confidential) that carries its own protection settings
A workspace role that controls which items a user can open
A DAX filter expression that restricts which rows a user sees
A tag that only exists inside Power BI and has no relationship to Office or email
questions.explain: A sensitivity label is Microsoft Purview Information Protection's classification tag, applied to Fabric items, and it reuses the same labels used for Office documents and email.

questions.q: In the Fabric portal, what is the fastest way to view or change an open item's sensitivity label?
options: Selecting the sensitivity bar in the item's header to open the label flyout
Editing the item's underlying DAX measures
Opening the Fabric admin portal's capacity settings
Sensitivity labels can only be changed from Power BI Desktop, never in the service
questions.explain: The sensitivity bar sits in the item's header next to its name; selecting it opens a flyout showing the current label with a dropdown to change it. The same control is also available in the item's Settings pane.

questions.q: Where are default and mandatory label policies for Fabric and Power BI actually configured?
options: Centrally, in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal
Individually, on each report's Settings pane
In the Fabric admin portal's capacity settings
They cannot be configured — only applied manually, item by item
questions.explain: Both default label policies (pre-filling new content with a starting label) and mandatory label policies (blocking unlabeled saves) are built in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal's label policy wizard, not inside Fabric itself.

questions.q: A sensitivity label is applied to a semantic model with downstream inheritance enabled. What happens to the reports and dashboards built on top of it?
options: The label automatically propagates to them, unless they already carry a manually applied or more restrictive label
Nothing — labels never propagate between items in Fabric
They are deleted and must be rebuilt with the new label
The label only propagates if each downstream item is re-published from Power BI Desktop
questions.explain: Downstream inheritance automatically applies a parent item's label to everything built from it, but it never overwrites a manually applied label and never replaces a label with a less restrictive one.

questions.q: What happens to a sensitivity label when a labeled Power BI report is exported to Excel, PDF, or PowerPoint?
options: Power BI stamps the exported file with the same label and applies its protection settings
The label and its protections are stripped automatically on export
The export is always blocked, regardless of the label
The label only carries over if the file is exported as CSV
questions.explain: Export to Excel, PDF, or PowerPoint, Analyze in Excel, and .pbix download are supported export paths — the exported file is automatically stamped with the source label and its protection settings. Unsupported paths like CSV don't carry the label.
